# Working Title
TCAC 2.0 — Transformative Change Assessment Corpus 2.0

## Code repo

[Github repository](https://github.com/IPBES-Data/TCAC-2.0)

# Introduction

The literature search for the Transformative Change assessment corpus was conducted using search terms provided by the experts and refined in co-operation with the IPBES task force for data and knowledge management.
The search was conducted using [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org), scripted from [R](https://cran.r-project.org) to use  the [OpenAlex API](https://docs.openalex.org). Search terms for the following searches were defined:

- **Transformative Change**,
- **Nature / Environment**
- **case studies** and 
- **additional search terms** for specific corpora

To assess the quality of the corpus, sets of key papers were selected by the experts to verify if these are in the corpus. 
These key papers were selected per chapter / sub-chapter to ensure that the corpus is representative of each chapter.  

The following terminology is used in this document:

- **Corpus**: A body of works as based on a search on [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org)
- **Transformative Change Assessment Corpus**: Short: TCA corpus; The corpus resulting from the search terms `transformative AND nature`
- **Case corpus**: The corpus resulting from `transformative AND nature AND case`
- **work**: terminology used for a single document in their datasewt. Each work has a unique OpenAlex id, but not necesarily a DOI.

The following searches are conducted on Title and Abstract only as the availability of fulltexts drops in 2020. OpenAlex "inherited" their initial corpus from Microsoft Academic, which contained a many fulltext articles. After that initial start, other sources were used which did not all include fulltext versions. To eliminate a bias towards fulltext articles, we limited the search to abstracts and titles only.

# Results

## Assessment of Search Terms Using OpenAlex

### Number of Hits per Individual Corpus

Number of works returned by each individual search-term query and by
the combined `(nature) AND (transformative change)` query, before and
after the OpenAlex work-type filter is applied (only the types in
`input/openalex_types.csv` with `Included = TRUE` are kept).

```{r}
#| label: hits-per-search-term
cnt <- readRDS(tar_read(count_st))

# pro_request(count_only = TRUE) returns one row per query with `count`
# and `query`; the query column carries the named list element name.
labels <- c(
  tfc_complete = "Transformative Change — all types",
  tfc_filtered = "Transformative Change — filtered",
  nature_complete = "Nature — all types",
  nature_filtered = "Nature — filtered",
  tca_complete = "Assessment Corpus (combined) — all types",
  tca_filtered = "Assessment Corpus (combined) — filtered"
)

dplyr::tibble(
  search = labels[as.character(cnt$query)],
  count = as.integer(cnt$count)
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = "Number of works matching each search on OpenAlex. *filtered* applies the work-type filter; *all types* does not."
  )
```

The actual corpus extracted from the snapshot (after the type filter):

```{r}
#| label: tbl-corpus-size
tibble::tibble(
  corpus = "TCAC 2.0",
  `Works extracted` = nrow(arrow::open_dataset(tar_read(corpus_tcac20)))
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    align = c("l", "r"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )
```

## TCA Corpus properties

### Publications over time

Bars: yearly count of works in the TCAC 2.0 corpus. Red line:
cumulative proportion of the corpus. Blue line: cumulative proportion
of *all* of OpenAlex over the same year range — a useful baseline for
"is the corpus skewing recent vs the literature as a whole?". Both
cumulative lines use the secondary (right-hand) axis.

```{r}
#| label: publications-over-time
years <- arrow::open_dataset(tar_read(corpus_tcac20)) |>
  dplyr::count(publication_year) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(publication_year), publication_year >= 1900) |>
  dplyr::arrange(publication_year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p = n / sum(n),
    p_cum = cumsum(p)
  )

# OpenAlex universe baseline (from yearly_counts target, label =
# "openalex_universe"). Recompute its cumulative proportion over the
# same year window as the corpus so the two lines are comparable.
oa_universe <- readRDS(tar_read(yearly_counts)) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    label == "openalex_universe",
    publication_year %in% years$publication_year
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(publication_year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_oa = count / sum(count),
    p_oa_cum = cumsum(p_oa)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(publication_year, p_oa, p_oa_cum)

ymax <- max(years$n)

ggplot2::ggplot(years, ggplot2::aes(x = publication_year)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(y = n), fill = "#BBBBBB") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    ggplot2::aes(y = p_cum * ymax),
    colour = "red",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = oa_universe,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = p_oa_cum * ymax),
    colour = "blue",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Number of works per year (bars)",
    sec.axis = ggplot2::sec_axis(
      ~ . / ymax,
      name = "Cumulative proportion (red = corpus, blue = OpenAlex universe)"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Publication year") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
